text:
Alex Newhook has 6 goals and 11 points in 23 games, and his finishing is exactly what it should be: 6 goals on 5.98 expected (the quality of his chances). He plays about 16 minutes a night in Montreal's middle six and has a Stanley Cup ring from his Colorado days.

The concern is the other end. At five on five the Canadiens get only 41.8% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 12.2 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey made a similar point last season, with Montreal creating fewer chances than usual when he played (bottom 9% of forwards).

So Newhook is a useful scorer in a secondary role who doesn't tilt the ice. His ice time has nudged up in the last two games, and he scored a patient tying goal in Carolina on Thursday, as Karine Hains of The Hockey News noted. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck, a decent sign. Watch his line's shot share: if it climbs, the role grows.
headline: Newhook scores enough; the chances against are the worry
